claims.text: Low-dimensional structure induces magnetic anisotropy in as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy thin films or nanoribbons.
Reduced dimensionality enhances thermal fluctuations in these alloy thin films or nanoribbons.
Competition between magnetic anisotropy and thermal fluctuations governs the magnetocaloric response.
Competition between magnetic anisotropy and thermal fluctuations governs magnetic hysteresis.
A controlled low-amplitude magnetic field, exemplified by 100 Oe, is the proposed intervention during cooling cycles.
Lower cooling rates will enhance the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Lower cycle frequencies will enhance the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Lower cooling rates will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Lower cycle frequencies will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The proposed operating ranges are cooling rates of 0.1–10 K/s, cycle frequencies of 0.1–10 Hz, and magnetic-field amplitudes of 0–1000 Oe.
Heat-transfer rate may limit the accessible magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
A lack of significant dependence of magnetocaloric response and hysteresis on cooling rate and cycle frequency would falsify the hypothesis.
